title: What Came Before the Watchful Gods? — Tylor’s (1871) Animism Question, Mace & Pagel Phylogenetic Comparative Methods & Peoples, Duda & Marlowe’s (2016) Bayesian Ancestral Reconstruction Across 33 Hunter-Gatherer Societies

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Did moralizing 'Big Gods' come first in human religion, or spirits and ancestors? By mapping 33 hunter-gatherer societies onto a language family tree, Peoples, Duda & Marlowe (2016) reconstructed deep prehistory: animism came first, followed by afterlife, shamanism, and ancestor worship—long before watchful high gods.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Cross-cultural counts get fooled when cousin societies inherit traits from one shared ancestor ('Galton's problem'); Bayesian phylogenetic trees turn ethnography into testable evolutionary timelines.
keyTakeaways: Edward Burnett Tylor (1871) proposed animism—belief in spiritual beings—as religion's earliest foundation, whereas later theories debated high gods and moral enforcement.
Mace and Pagel showed why cross-cultural comparisons must model trait changes along linguistic/genetic phylogenies rather than treating neighboring societies as independent data points.

Across 33 hunter-gatherer societies, Peoples, Duda & Marlowe (2016) found animism present in every group, reconstructing sequential emergence of afterlife beliefs, shamanism, and ancestor spirits—while active moralizing 'high gods' were rare or absent in ancestral foraging bands.

vocab.meaning: Belief that natural phenomena, animals, plants, or places possess spiritual agency or souls (Tylor 1871).
Statistical non-independence among societies that share cultural traits through common ancestry or borrowing rather than independent invention.
Estimating continuous-time Markov transition rates of cultural traits along a phylogeny to infer deep-node probabilities.

quiz.question: In Peoples, Duda & Marlowe's (2016) phylogenetic study of 33 hunter-gatherer societies, which religious trait reconstructed as oldest and universal, and which was rarest?
options: Active moralizing high gods were universal and animism was absent
Animism was universal/oldest, while active moralizing high gods were rare and late-emerging
Shamanism only appeared after industrial agriculture
quiz.explanation: Animism was present across all 33 hunter-gatherer societies and reconstructed at the root, whereas active high gods appeared in very few foraging societies.
